vectors.spec_section: KERI field labels (s: Sequence Number). The spec does not define the /ksn route itself, so this rests on the generic s rule and on keripy interop
vectors.spec_quote: |`s`| Sequence Number | strictly monotonically increasing integer encoded in hex |

vectors.description: the same key state notice with a.s="10" (sn 10 written in decimal, which reads as hex 0x10 = 16) and d the SAID of the sn-10 event
vectors.reason: there is no event at sn 0x10; the notice is inconsistent with the KEL
vectors.spec_section: KERI field labels (s: Sequence Number). The spec does not define the /ksn route itself, so this rests on the generic s rule and on keripy interop
vectors.spec_quote: |`s`| Sequence Number | strictly monotonically increasing integer encoded in hex |

keripy.note: keripy accepts it: processReplyKeyStateNotice compares d with the KEL only when it has an event at the notice's sn (src/keri/core/eventing.py:5317-5326), and there is none at 0x10

vectors.description: a witnessed inception and the witness's key state notice reply in keripy's shape ({vn:[1,0], i, s, p, d, f, dt, et, kt, k, nt, n, bt, b, c, ee, di}), signed with the witness's couple
vectors.reason: a key state notice from a designated witness that matches the KEL
vectors.spec_section: Reply Message Body (the spec defines no ksn / key state notice)
vectors.spec_quote: The top-level fields of a Reply, `rpy` message body MUST appear in the following order: `[ v, t, d, dt, r, a]`. All are REQUIRED.
vectors.ambiguity: The specification does not define the key state notice; keripy's KeyStateRecord is the de facto shape.

vectors.description: two /loc/scheme replies of the non-transferable eid B with the same dt, the first with url http://a/, the second with http://evil/, each signed with B's couple
vectors.reason: an update is accepted only when its date-time is later than the prior's
vectors.spec_quote:
IF both the Update’s and the Prior's key-states appear at the same location in KEL AND...
        the Update’s date-time is later than the Prior's date-time THEN accept.
  Otherwise, do not accept.

vectors.description: the controller's inception; /end/role/add {cid:C, role:watcher, eid:W} at :11 and /end/role/cut for the same at :12, both signed by C; then the :11 add again
vectors.reason: the cut nullifies the authorization; the replayed older add is stale
vectors.spec_section: RUN off the CRUD / Player EID in Role by CID Nullify Via Cut
vectors.spec_quote: Instead of Delete, Peers Nullify. A Nullify is a special type of Update that indicates that the data in the record is no longer valid but, importantly, without actually erasing or Deleting the record that includes a reference to the latest monotonic determining anchor and/or date-time.

vectors.description: the controller's inception; /end/role/add {cid:C, role:witness, eid:A} at :10, then {cid:C, role:witness, eid:B} at :00, both signed by C
vectors.reason: each (cid, role, eid) is its own record; B has no prior to be compared with
vectors.spec_section: BADA Rules / OOBI KERI Endpoint Authorization (OKEA)
vectors.spec_quote: The BADA rules apply to any data item stored in a database record whose value is used for some defined purpose.

vectors.description: the controller's inception and /end/role/add {cid:C, role:registrar, eid:R} signed by C
vectors.reason: registrar is a role an AID may play
vectors.spec_section: OOBI URL (IURL) / OOBI KERI Endpoint Authorization (OKEA)
vectors.spec_quote: The AID may act in any of the KERI roles such as `watcher`, `witness`, `juror`, `judge` or `registrar` but is usually a `controller`.
vectors.ambiguity: The specification names watcher, witness, juror, judge and registrar as examples of roles ("such as"); it does not enumerate the role values.

vectors.description: the controller's inception and /end/role/add {cid:C, role:mailbox, eid:R} signed by C
vectors.reason: mailbox is a role an AID may play
vectors.spec_section: OOBI URL (IURL) / OOBI KERI Endpoint Authorization (OKEA)
vectors.spec_quote: The AID may act in any of the KERI roles such as `watcher`, `witness`, `juror`, `judge` or `registrar` but is usually a `controller`.
vectors.ambiguity: mailbox is a keripy role (keriox calls it messagebox); the specification does not enumerate role values, so whether it is valid is unspecified.

vectors.description: a /loc/scheme reply of eid B for https at :11, then one with url "" at :12, both signed with B's couple
vectors.reason: an empty url nullifies the location
vectors.spec_section: Endpoint Location with Scheme by EID Nullify Via Empty URL
vectors.spec_quote: To Nullify set the `url` to the empty string `""`.

vectors.description: a /loc/scheme reply for eid=D... (transferable Ed25519 code) with a non-transferable receipt couple (D key, valid signature)
vectors.reason: a transferable AID must sign with a reference to its key state; only a non-transferable code has a fixed key state
vectors.spec_quote: In this case, the update MUST either includes a reference to the Key-state in the authorizing AID's KEL from which the signing keypair(s) needed to verify the signature is obtained or the AID MUST be ephemeral with a fixed Key-state (has a non-transferable derivation code).

vectors.description: a /loc/scheme reply of eid B (Ed25519) whose receipt couple carries B with B's valid Ed25519 signature bytes coded 0C (ECDSA secp256k1)
vectors.reason: the signature does not verify against the key; the reply is rejected (a validator must not crash)
vectors.spec_quote: Confirm signature on the Update verifies against indicated key-state under which signature was made.

keripy.note: keripy verifies the signature bytes with the key's algorithm and ignores the signature code (Cigar.verfer.verify), so it accepts the reply

vectors.description: a /loc/scheme reply of eid B (Ed25519) whose receipt couple carries B with 64 random bytes coded 0C (ECDSA secp256k1)
vectors.reason: the signature does not verify against the key; the reply is rejected (a validator must not crash)
vectors.spec_quote: Confirm signature on the Update verifies against indicated key-state under which signature was made.

vectors.description: a /loc/scheme reply whose version string names the ACDC protocol (size and SAID correct), signed with the eid's couple
vectors.reason: the protocol of a KERI message is KERI
vectors.spec_quote: To elaborate, the protocol field, `PPPP` value in the Version String MUST be `KERI` for the KERI protocol.

vectors.description: a KERI 1.0 exn /fwd (keripy's shape [v,t,d,i,rp,p,dt,r,q,a,e]) embedding an inception, whose only attachment is the pathed group with the embedded event's signature; no sender signature
vectors.reason: an exchange message must carry its sender's signature
vectors.spec_quote: Signatures and Seals MUST be attached to the Message body using CESR attachment codes.

vectors.description: an exn /fwd in keriox's shape [v,t,d,dt,r,q,a] with the inception in a, whose only attachment is the pathed group with the embedded event's signature; no sender signature
vectors.reason: an exchange message must carry its sender's signature (and this body also lacks the required i field)
vectors.spec_quote: Signatures and Seals MUST be attached to the Message body using CESR attachment codes.
